\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سر} \fa{و} \fa{صدا} (sar-o sedâ)}{سر و صدا (sar-o sedâ)}]{\fa{سر} \fa{و} \fa{صدا} (sar-o sedâ) — noise, a din}

\label{lesson:FA-C440-sar-o-seda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for central heating, then the Persian for a view.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سر} \fa{و} \fa{صدا}}
\textbf{\fa{سر} \fa{و} \fa{صدا}} (\emph{sar-o sedâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}noise, a din\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اتاق} \fa{ما} \fa{شب} \fa{پر} \fa{از} \fa{سر} \fa{و} \fa{صدا} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Otâq-e mâ shab por az sar-o sedâ bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our room was full of noise at night.
\end{quote}

\emph{Sar-o sedâ kardan} — to make a racket. Also a fuss: \emph{sar-o sedâ-ye ziyâdi kard} — it caused a stir.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sar-o sedâ} is a pair of native \emph{sar} 'head', from Middle Persian \emph{sar} (EtymDB), and \emph{sedâ} 'sound', which EtymDB takes from Arabic \emph{ṣadā} 'echo'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sar-o sedâ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sar-o sedâ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sar-o sedâ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for central heating, then the Persian for a view, then say \emph{sar-o sedâ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{سر} \fa{و} \fa{صدا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Noise, a din\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کثیف} (kasif)}{کثیف (kasif)}]{\fa{کثیف} (kasif) — dirty}

\label{lesson:FA-C440-kasif}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a view, then the Persian for noise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کثیف}}
\textbf{\fa{کثیف}} (\emph{kasif}) — \textquotedblleft{}dirty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{حوله} \fa{های} \fa{حمام} \fa{کثیف} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hole-hâ-ye hammâm kasif bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bathroom towels were dirty.
\end{quote}

The opposite of \emph{tamiz}. Note the letter \fa{ث}, said \emph{s}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kasif} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{kaṯīf} (EtymDB). In Arabic the word usually means 'thick, dense'; in Persian the sense moved to 'dirty'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kasif}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kasif}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kasif}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a view, then the Persian for noise, then say \emph{kasif} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صدا} \fa{دادن} (sedâ dâdan)}{صدا دادن (sedâ dâdan)}]{\fa{صدا} \fa{دادن} (sedâ dâdan) — to make a noise, to squeak, to rattle}

\label{lesson:FA-C440-seda-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for noise, then the Persian for dirty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صدا} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{صدا} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{sedâ dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to make a noise, to squeak, to rattle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{اتاق} \fa{موقع} \fa{باز} \fa{شدن} \fa{صدا} \fa{میدهد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar-e otâq mowqe'-e bâz shodan sedâ midahad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The room's door squeaks when it opens.
\end{quote}

\emph{sedâ} 'sound' + \emph{dâdan} 'to give'. Present stem \emph{dah-}: \emph{sedâ midahad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sedâ dâdan} is built from \emph{sedâ} 'sound', which EtymDB takes from Arabic \emph{ṣadā} 'echo', and \emph{dâdan} 'to give', which EtymDB traces to the PIE root \emph{deh\textsubscript{3}-} 'to give'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for noise, then the Persian for dirty, then say \emph{sedâ dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بدبو} (badbu)}{بدبو (badbu)}]{\fa{بدبو} (badbu) — smelly, foul-smelling}

\label{lesson:FA-C440-badbu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for dirty, then the Persian for to make a noise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بدبو}}
\textbf{\fa{بدبو}} (\emph{badbu}) — \textquotedblleft{}smelly, foul-smelling\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آب} \fa{لوله} \fa{بدبو} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Âb-e lule badbu bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The tap water smelled bad.
\end{quote}

\emph{bad} 'bad' + \emph{bu} 'smell'; the opposite of \emph{khoshbu}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{badbu} is a native compound of \emph{bad} 'bad' and \emph{bu} 'smell', the word behind \emph{buyidan} 'to smell'. EtymDB does not list the compound.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آب} \fa{گرمکن} (âbgarmkon)}{آب گرمکن (âbgarmkon)}]{\fa{آب} \fa{گرمکن} (âbgarmkon) — a water heater, a boiler}

\label{lesson:FA-C440-abgarmkon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to make a noise, then the Persian for smelly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آب} \fa{گرمکن}}
\textbf{\fa{آب} \fa{گرمکن}} (\emph{âbgarmkon}) — \textquotedblleft{}a water heater, a boiler\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آب} \fa{گرمکن} \fa{خراب} \fa{بود} \fa{و} \fa{آب} \fa{حمام} \fa{سرد} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Âbgarmkon kharâb bud va âb-e hammâm sard bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The water heater was broken and the bath water was cold.
\end{quote}

\emph{âb} 'water' + \emph{garm} 'hot' + \emph{kon} 'making'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âbgarmkon} is a native compound: \emph{âb} 'water' goes back to Middle Persian \emph{āb} (EtymDB), \emph{garm} 'warm' is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{garm}, and \emph{kon} is the present stem of \emph{kardan} 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
